title: Recovery from coinduced Cech pieces in a product-closed triangulated class
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring, $V$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, and $N$ an actual module for its pulled-back coefficient $\Lambda_V$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\{b_i:U_i\to V\}_{i\in I}$ be a small pro-etale covering family with every $U_i$ affine [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention, lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Let $P$ be any full replete triangulated object property of the ordinary derived module category of $V$, closed under all small derived products [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory, def-weil-category-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that for every $i$, every quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $W$ and every weakly etale quasi-compact quasi-separated $r:W\to U_i$ [sk-def-pe-morphisms, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $$P\bigl(R(r b_i)_*((r^*b_i^*N)[0])\bigr).$$ The inverse images and direct image are the actual coefficient-compatible module operations [def-sfb-module-upper-star, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Then $P(N[0])$. The hypothesis includes all finite Cech intersections over $V$, which need not be affine or weakly contractible. This theorem concerns an arbitrary class $P$; it does not assert stability of any generated hull under pullback or pushforward, nor require filtered-colimit or retract closure. No coefficient admissibility or weak-contractibility hypothesis is imposed. The empty scheme and empty covering, zero ring, zero module and identity covering are included.

proof.text: If $V$ is empty, its module category is zero and triangulated zero and repleteness prove the assertion. Otherwise take a finite affine refinement of the given covering. Replacing each refinement member by its original $U_i$ still gives a covering: every affine test's finite quasi-compact covering refinement for the smaller family is also a refinement for the enlarged family. Thus retain a finite list $U_1,\ldots,U_t$ of the original affine objects. Each $b_i$ is qcqs by affine qcqs and qcqs morphism permanence. Every finite fibre product $U_{i_0\ldots i_n}$ over $V$ is a qcqs site object, by the finite-cover subsite geometry. In particular all its projections to $V$ and to $U_{i_0}$ are qcqs by the same permanence result. No assertion that these intersections are affine or weakly contractible is used.

proof.text: Apply the coherent augmented Cech pushforward model to the identity morphism and the epimorphic cover sheaf formed from the finite list. Its total represents $N[0]$. Each column is the finite product over index tuples of $R(r b_{i_0})_*((r^*b_{i_0}^*N)[0])$, where $r$ projects the corresponding intersection to $U_{i_0}$. All intersections and projections are qcqs and weakly etale by finite-family geometry. Slice localization and internal module transport identify the actual coefficients and restrictions, and finite-product injective resolutions give the derived column comparison. The hypothesis therefore puts every factor in $P$; product closure and repleteness put the columns in $P$.

Put $T_m=\operatorname{Tot}(B^{n,q}:0\le n\le m)$, with the horizontal differential out of column $m$ discarded. These are quotient complexes of the full total, with chain projections $T_m\to T_{m-1}$. Their kernels are the column $B^{m,\bullet}[-m]$, with vertical differential $(-1)^m d$. The degreewise short exact sequence gives the distinguished triangle with this column and the two successive $T$'s. Induction from $T_0=B^{0,\bullet}$, using the preceding step, shifts and extensions, gives $P(QT_m)$ for all $m$.

The projections of the tower $T_m$ split as maps of graded modules. Its termwise limit is $T=\operatorname{Tot}B$, since in total degree $r$ only $0\le n\le r$ occur. There is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes $0\to T\to\prod_mT_m\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_mT_m\to0$, where $(sx)_m$ is the projection of $x_{m+1}$. To see epimorphy, choose $x_0=0$ and recursively choose $x_{m+1}$ projecting to $x_m-y_m$ using the graded splitting; its kernel consists exactly of compatible sequences. The products represent derived products. Each belongs to $P$ by the preceding step; the short-exact triangle, rotation and shift closure put $QT$ in $P$. The augmented-total isomorphism in the second step yields $P(N[0])$.

theorem proetale_cech_product_class_recovery
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ]
    (V : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace V] [QuasiSeparatedSpace V]
    (N : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology V) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ V))
    (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → V.ProEt)
    (hcover : Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ (U i).left) (fun i ↦ (U i).hom) ∈
      Scheme.proetalePrecoverage.coverings V)
    (haffine : ∀ i : I, IsAffine (U i).left)
    (P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory
      (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology V) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ V))))
    (htri : P.IsTriangulated) (hiso : P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms)
    (hprod : ∀ (J : Type (u + 1))
      (K : J → DerivedCategory
        (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology V) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ V)))
      (c : Cone (Discrete.functor K)), IsLimit c → (∀ j : J, P (K j)) → P c.pt)
    (hpieces : ∀ (i : I) (W : Scheme.{u})
      [CompactSpace W] [QuasiSeparatedSpace W]
      (r : W ⟶ (U i).left) [WeaklyEtale r] [QuasiCompact r] [QuasiSeparated r],
      P ((CondensedRing.moduleObjectDerivedPushforward Λ (r ≫ (U i).hom)).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ r).obj
            ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ (U i).hom).obj N))))) :
    P ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)
